title: Half-length Nth 2-adic complexity for nine deterministic sequences
summary: Prove the half-length asymptotic Nth 2-adic complexity profile for four Thue-Morse samples, four Rudin-Shapiro samples, and the Zeckendorf digit-sum sequence.

formal_statement.body: For each sequence $S$ in the following nine-instance set: Thue-Morse sampled along $X,X^2,X^3,X^4$; Rudin-Shapiro sampled along $X,X^2,X^3,X^4$; and the binary Zeckendorf digit-sum sequence, prove that there exist constants $C_S,N_S>0$ such that $|\Phi_2(S,N)-N/2|\le C_S\log N$ for every $N\ge N_S$, or refute this bound for that instance. Settle all nine instances.

scope.domain: Nth 2-adic complexity of fixed aperiodic binary pseudorandom sequences
assumptions: Phi_2(S,N) is the source-defined Nth 2-adic complexity
Polynomial sampling uses X, X^2, X^3, or X^4 on nonnegative integers
Each of the nine deterministic sequence instances is settled separately
scope.unresolved_remainder: All nine deterministic instances remain unresolved. Later expected-value and almost-sure half-length theorems quantify over random sequences, and later algebraic-sequence results do not apply to these fixed automatic and Zeckendorf sequences.

citations.label: Chen--Chen--Obrovsky--Winterhof, deterministic Nth 2-adic conjecture
citations.locator: Section II, empirical conjecture, journal p. 6062

progress.summary: After computation through N=1,000,000, the source conjectures the half-length logarithmic-error profile separately for all nine named deterministic sequences.
